comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C2, C3, C24, C25 about C. glabrata pho2Δ strains retaining phosphatase activity and surviving phosphate limitation. Both find these claims SUPPORTED by experimental data in Figure 1A-B.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C32-C34 about potential convergent evolution in Y. lipolytica. Both find claims SUPPORTED while acknowledging the authors' appropriate caveats about ancestral vs. derived state.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C35-C36 about graded Pho2-independence as a quantitative trait. Peer reviewer explicitly notes the quantitative nature could be discussed further, while both find claims SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate RNA-seq data supporting claims about Pho2-dependence and target gene numbers (C5, C37-C43, C46-C47). Peer reviewer confirms statistical analysis is solid and claims are SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C44-C45 about expression level controls. Both find this control experiment SUPPORTED and important for ruling out confounding variables.
Strong agreement. Both evaluate ChIP-seq data on DNA binding (C6, C48-C53, C58). Both find claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewer confirming genomic approaches support the conclusions.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate claims C54-C55 about differential Pho2-dependence of DNA binding. Both find claims SUPPORTED as central to the accepted model, though peer result also includes C57 and C65.
Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claims C59-C61 about nucleosome occupancy analysis. Both find claims SUPPORTED with solid statistical analysis and experimental approach.
Strong agreement. Both evaluate integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data (C62-C65, C67). Both find the quantitative differences SUPPORTED and well-demonstrated by the data.
Strong agreement. Both evaluate ChIP-exo data in native C. glabrata context (C68-C75). Both find claims SUPPORTED, validating heterologous expression findings.
Perfect agreement. Both evaluate mutant cycle analysis (C76-C79) demonstrating shift in regulatory logic. Both find the methodological approach solid and claims SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate GO enrichment analysis and target expansion (C7, C80-C87). Peer reviewer explicitly confirms the conclusion about expanded stress response pathways is well supported by data. Both find claims SUPPORTED.
Agreement on support. OpenEval evaluates C87 about species-specific regulatory evolution. Peer result covers broader set (C81-C87) but includes this claim. Both find SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate main conclusions (C8, C94, C99, C102) about loss of Pho2-dependence enabling target expansion. Both explicitly state these conclusions are well SUPPORTED by comprehensive evidence.

Strong agreement. Both evaluate claims C88-C92 about conservation of core regulatory features. Both find claims SUPPORTED, with peer reviewer accepting the contrast between conserved features and divergent targets.

Agreement on support. Both evaluate C93 about gene conservation vs. functional importance. OpenEval also includes C95 about CgPho4 being 'stronger'. Both find claims SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about mechanism.

Agreement on support. OpenEval evaluates C95 about CgPho4 functional properties. Peer result includes C93 and C95. Both find claims SUPPORTED while acknowledging mechanistic details remain to be elucidated.
Agreement on support. Both evaluate C96-C98 about network plasticity. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate contextualization. Peer reviewer confirms C96 is well supported by data.

Agreement on uncertainty. OpenEval evaluates C100-C101 about evolutionary timescales and finds competing claims (rapid vs. gradual) with C100 being speculative, rating UNCERTAIN. Peer result evaluates C97, C100, C103 as explicitly speculative, rating UNCERTAIN.

Divergent evaluation. OpenEval evaluates C103 about altered Pho4-Pho2 interaction as proof-of-principle and finds it SUPPORTED. Peer result groups C103 with speculative claims C97, C100 and rates UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic questions remain open.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty. Both evaluate claims C104-C112 about virulence and pathogenesis connections. Both find these speculative, lacking experimental validation in C. glabrata, and rate UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1, C9-C23, C26-C27) from prior literature and preliminary findings, finding them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational context claims.
